items.q: Fill up: The Cockcroft & Gault equation was developed when creatinine was estimated by the ______ method, a colorimetric assay using alkaline picrate.
items.exp: The disadvantage table states the equation was developed when Cr was estimated by Jaffe's method: colorimetric assay using alkaline picrate, flagged as not a standard method. (Book p735)

items.q: All of the following are stated about creatinine on this page EXCEPT:
opts: It is the best marker to estimate GFR
It is produced in muscle from creatine
Its value falls when muscle mass is reduced
items.exp: Creatinine is printed as an 113 kDa molecule; 13 kDa is the cystatin C molecule described on p737. (Book p735)

items.q: The page marks pregnancy as the only condition in which high creatinine values are significant independently, with a normal range of 0.3–0.6 mg/dL.
opts: True — and the quoted pregnancy range is 0.3–0.6 mg/dL
False — the same independence is claimed for cirrhosis
False — pregnancy never yields significant creatinine values
True — but the quoted range is 0.6–1.2 mg/dL
items.exp: Bullet: 'Pregnancy: Only condition where high creatinine values significant independently (Normal: 0.3–0.6 mg/dL)'. (Book p735)

items.q: A bilateral above-knee amputee has a serum creatinine of 0.8 mg/dL although the true GFR is clearly reduced. Which property of creatinine printed here explains the normal value?
opts: Reduced muscle mass lowers creatinine production
Increased tubular secretion compensates for the loss
Dilution from post-operative fluids masks the rise
The assay under-reads in non-pregnant adults
items.exp: Creatinine is produced in muscle from creatine and is reduced when muscle mass is reduced — the book's own example is amputation, so a low production rate hides the fall in GFR. (Book p735)
